title: Video | Is diesel really the copper miners’ biggest cost worry?
gist: Wood Mackenzie's Mined Over Matter episode argues rising diesel prices after the US-Iran conflict that began in March are not necessarily copper miners' biggest cost worry: strong copper and by-product prices help absorb the pressure, and exposure varies by region and mine type. Skilled labour shortages and wages in Chile, acid costs, contract renegotiations, declining ore grades and complex ore bodies could weigh more on costs and supply in 2027.

themes.theme: Diesel cost pressure from Middle East conflict

insights.claim: Disruption in the Middle East following the US-Iran conflict that began in March has put energy costs back on the agenda for copper miners, with rising diesel prices increasingly cited in updated cost guidance.
insights.speaker: Alex Griffiths
insights.so_what: Watch copper miners' cost guidance revisions for diesel-related escalation tied to Middle East supply risk.

insights.claim: Diesel exposure differs between open-pit and underground copper mines, so the impact of higher diesel prices varies significantly by region and mine type.
insights.speaker: Alex Griffiths
insights.so_what: Open-pit-heavy producers are more exposed to fuel prices; screen portfolios by mining method when assessing diesel sensitivity.

insights.claim: Strong copper and by-product prices are helping producers absorb diesel cost pressure, making the industry's current position different from previous periods of energy cost inflation.
insights.speaker: Alex Griffiths
insights.so_what: Margin compression from energy inflation may be less severe than headlines suggest while copper prices stay strong.
